$comment: CR-W (proposed protocol.md §11.50) wire vectors for emulator/screen_text's `panel` kind and its initialize.capabilities.screenTextKinds rider, authored by the oracle lane against empyrean origin/main 610d0c70 (contract/ unchanged from fedb881a). Tags: [CR-W core] is the kind, the `panel` key and the if/then that ties them; [CR-W rider R1] is droppable, and its reds PASS without its patch (measured, CR section 8). PROVENANCE, STATED PLAINLY: every screen_text document here is HAND-BUILT. The drafting parcel was barred from running an emulator or opening the window, so no panel reply exists to capture; the column heads come from crates/oracle-player/src/stopping.rs:169-194, the no-label marker from stopping.rs:346, the tab titles from ui.rs Tab::title, the refusal from CR-H's live capture. CR-H's bar applies: the implementing parcel replaces cases 1-4 with real replies before the method serves the kind. RESIDUE a document schema cannot see, all SERVER BEHAVIOUR and all conformance rows in the CR (section 9, W1-W10): that a panel surface exists exactly when its body was drawn, that `text` and `rendered` share joins at the same run boundaries, that `rendered` is the toolkit's glyphs rather than a restated fit, that an unclipped unelided run has rendered == text, and that `unrenderable` names real hollow boxes. RUN: each case was judged against the upstream fragment and two patched variants (core, core+R1) with the upstream validator's own closure composition, and appended to the upstream vectors for a whole-gate run per variant; verdicts in the CR, section 8. Case 5 is an error document, which empyrean G3 has no arm for; it was judged against $defs/errorObject and is for oracle's harness (check_incoming_strict), as CR-H's refusal was.

cases.why: [CR-W core] §11.50 - THE POPULATED REPLY. Two leaves are expanded, so two panel bodies were drawn this present, each one surface named by its tab title; the hidden tabs sharing those leaves are absent because their bodies did not run (egui_dock-0.21.1 leaf.rs:1330). Breakpoints' last column was squeezed by fit_columns and the toolkit elided one cell: `rendered` carries the elision mark, so `truncated` derives true, and because both strings share their TAB/LF joins at the same run boundaries, row 4 run 6 is the cell that was cut. The cell's hover (ui.rs table_cell) is NOT a surface: it is on the glass only while hovered, and `text` already carries the full source. Hand-built (see the file's $comment); the implementing parcel replaces it with a real reply.

[CR-W core] §11.50 - EVERY LEAF COLLAPSED (reachable: layout.rs records fully_collapsed). No panel body ran, so no panel surface, and the reply is a valid pre-CR-W reply byte for byte. This is exactly the ambiguity rider R1 exists for: without `capabilities.screenTextKinds` a client cannot tell this reply from one by a server that never reports panels. Hand-built (see the file's $comment); the implementing parcel replaces it with a real reply.

[CR-W core] §11.50 - A PANEL WHOSE BODY WAS DRAWN WITH NO TEXT ON THE GLASS is PRESENT with empty strings, never omitted. Per-panel granularity is chosen over per-line surfaces for this case: 'the panel is on screen and says nothing' and 'the panel is not on screen' must not be the same artifact (§11.29's refusal argument, one level down). Hand-built (see the file's $comment); the implementing parcel replaces it with a real reply.

[CR-W rider R1] §11.50 R1 - the player's deployment: the three kinds it can put on the glass. With this, case 2's panel-less reply reads as 'no panel is drawn', not 'panels are not reported'.
[CR-W rider R1] §11.50 R1 - a headless server: present and EMPTY, because it serves emulator/screen_text (and refuses it). Empty is a statement, absence means the server predates the key.
[CR-W rider R1] RED - a kind the method's own enum does not have; the two lists cannot drift.
[CR-W rider R1] RED - a boolean `panels: true`-style flag in the list's place; it cannot say which kinds, and a second flag per future kind is the growth the list avoids.
